# The Markdown gate. Named .markdownlint-cli2.yaml in a repository, where both
# the workflow step and a bare local `markdownlint-cli2` read it.
#
# The file list lives here rather than in the step, which passes an empty
# `globs` so this one is used: a step naming its own glob leaves a local run
# checking a different set of files from the gate.

# What CI sees is the checkout, which is the tracked files and nothing else: no
# node_modules, no vendor/, no .venv, no build output. A working copy has all of
# them, so without this a local run reports hundreds of findings in third-party
# Markdown that the gate will never look at, and `--fix` rewrites it in place.
gitignore: true

globs:
  - "**/*.md"

# Read alongside gitignore above, which does not cover everything the checkout
# leaves out. A submodule is tracked as a commit rather than as files, so CI
# checks out an empty directory while a working copy holds the whole upstream
# tree; gitignore says nothing about it, and a repository that adds one names it
# here. node_modules is named because it is not gitignored in every repository
# that has one. The trailing `**` is what excludes a tree: a glob ending at the
# directory name matches nothing and is dropped silently.
#
# The agent directories and instruction files are excluded by the global
# gitignore rather than by a repository's own, and gitignore above reads only
# the ones in the tree. So CI, which checks out tracked files, never sees them,
# while a working copy holds them and would report findings the gate cannot.
#
# A repository that commits its agent skills re-includes them in its own
# .gitignore, so CI does check them out and the gate should read them. It swaps
# the ".claude/**" line below for the pair
#
#   - ".claude/*"
#   - ".claude/!(skills)/**"
#
# which ignores the loose files and every subdirectory except skills/. The
# sweep accepts either spelling, but only whole: ".claude/*" on its own leaves
# every subdirectory linted. An entry is negated and handed to micromatch, so
# the extglob does the excepting; a leading "!" here would arrive as "!!" and
# re-include rather than exclude.
ignores:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - ".agents/**"
  - ".claude/**"
  - ".codex/**"
  - AGENTS.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - GEMINI.md

# Every rule markdownlint has, then what is given up and why.
config:
  # Line length, which defaults to 80. Tables and link-bearing prose here run
  # past any column worth setting, and rewrapping them buys nothing.
  MD013: false
  # Inline HTML. <kbd> marks up key names in the keybinding tables, and Markdown
  # has no equivalent, so this rule rejects correct markup rather than finding
  # anything wrong with it.
  MD033: false
  # Spaces inside emphasis. An asterisk here is usually a glob or a
  # multiplication sign, `*.glsl, *.glslp` and `Thickness * Width * Length`, and
  # the rule reads both as emphasis that someone padded. CommonMark does not:
  # neither closing asterisk is right-flanking, so none of it renders as
  # emphasis and there is nothing to correct. Left on, its fix closes the gap
  # and changes what the text says.
  MD037: false
  # Table pipe style, and pipe alignment. Both take their expected style from
  # the first table in a file, so one table decides for every other one, and a
  # single row brought into line flips the expectation and puts every remaining
  # table out. Neither changes what renders. A table whose first cell is empty
  # also cannot be written in the compact style most of these files use: the
  # row has to open with a pipe, which the rule then reads as a style break.
  #
  # MD056 stays on below: a row short of a cell silently drops data, which is
  # not a style question.
  MD055: false
  MD060: false
  # Duplicate headings, narrowed rather than turned off. A README that documents
  # two commands gives each an Example and a Usage under its own heading, which
  # the rule rejects by default because it compares against every heading in the
  # document. Restricted to siblings, it still catches the same name twice in
  # one section, which is the case that makes an anchor ambiguous.
  MD024:
    siblings_only: true

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# A newer run on the same ref cancels a superseded one. Runs on main and tags each get their own
# group, so none of them is cancelled or displaced while queued.
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')) && github.run_id || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Verification is capped at fifteen minutes: a job still running then
    # has hung rather than completed its bounded source and package checks.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
      - name: Set up Docker
        uses: docker/setup-docker-action@v5.7.0
        with:
          version: v29.9.3
      - name: Verify source and the local package in stock images
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source tests/container/stock
          stock_begin "$PWD"
          if [[ ! ${GITHUB_SHA:-} =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ || ${revision} != "${GITHUB_SHA:-}" || ${source_dirty} != false ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' 'CI requires clean source matching a full GITHUB_SHA.' >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          node_image=
          shellcheck_image=
          node_version=$(cat .nvmrc)
          stock_image node_image "node:${node_version#v}"
          stock_image shellcheck_image koalaman/shellcheck:v0.11.0
          stock_readonly "${shellcheck_image}" /bin/shellcheck -x -P SCRIPTDIR \
            tests/container/stock tests/container/check tests/container/node
          stock_prepare "${node_image}" node -- sh tests/container/node prepare
          stock_run "${node_image}" node -- sh tests/container/node check
          stock_finish
      - name: Install dependencies for the host release controller
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --maxsockets=1 --cache "$RUNNER_TEMP/game-kit-npm-cache"
      - name: Populate the offline release pack cache
        run: node scripts/npm-cache.ts load "$RUNNER_TEMP/game-kit-npm-cache"
      - name: Pack and prove the exact source release artifact
        run: |
          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          test -z "$(git status --porcelain)"
          node scripts/pack.ts .claude/release-output
          version=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
          SOURCE_COMMIT="$GITHUB_SHA" node scripts/release-artifact.ts \
            ".claude/release-output/game-kit-$version.tgz"
          test "$(cat .claude/release-output/SOURCE_COMMIT)" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
          (cd .claude/release-output && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7.0.2
        with:
          name: game-kit-${{ github.sha }}
          path: |
            .claude/release-output/game-kit-*.tgz
            .claude/release-output/SHA256SUMS
            .claude/release-output/SOURCE_COMMIT
          if-no-files-found: error
          include-hidden-files: true

# The Markdown gate. Named .markdownlint-cli2.yaml in a repository, where both
# the workflow step and a bare local `markdownlint-cli2` read it.
#
# The file list lives here rather than in the step, which passes an empty
# `globs` so this one is used: a step naming its own glob leaves a local run
# checking a different set of files from the gate.

# What CI sees is the checkout, which is the tracked files and nothing else: no
# node_modules, no vendor/, no .venv, no build output. A working copy has all of
# them, so without this a local run reports hundreds of findings in third-party
# Markdown that the gate will never look at, and `--fix` rewrites it in place.
gitignore: true

globs:
  - "**/*.md"

# Read alongside gitignore above, which does not cover everything the checkout
# leaves out. A submodule is tracked as a commit rather than as files, so CI
# checks out an empty directory while a working copy holds the whole upstream
# tree; gitignore says nothing about it, and a repository that adds one names it
# here. node_modules is named because it is not gitignored in every repository
# that has one. The trailing `**` is what excludes a tree: a glob ending at the
# directory name matches nothing and is dropped silently.
#
# The agent directories and instruction files are excluded by the global
# gitignore rather than by a repository's own, and gitignore above reads only
# the ones in the tree. So CI, which checks out tracked files, never sees them,
# while a working copy holds them and would report findings the gate cannot.
ignores:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - ".agents/**"
  - ".claude/**"
  - ".codex/**"
  - AGENTS.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - GEMINI.md
  # the ergogen submodules, whose Markdown is upstream's. Matched at any depth:
  # each revision directory symlinks to the one checkout, so the same files are
  # reachable under v1/ as well as at the path .gitmodules names.
  - "**/ergogen/footprints/**"
  - "**/ergogen/kb_ergogen_helper/**"

# Every rule markdownlint has, then what is given up and why.
config:
  # Line length, which defaults to 80. Tables and link-bearing prose here run
  # past any column worth setting, and rewrapping them buys nothing.
  MD013: false
  # Inline HTML. <kbd> marks up key names in the keybinding tables, and Markdown
  # has no equivalent, so this rule rejects correct markup rather than finding
  # anything wrong with it.
  MD033: false
  # Spaces inside emphasis. An asterisk here is usually a glob or a
  # multiplication sign, `*.glsl, *.glslp` and `Thickness * Width * Length`, and
  # the rule reads both as emphasis that someone padded. CommonMark does not:
  # neither closing asterisk is right-flanking, so none of it renders as
  # emphasis and there is nothing to correct. Left on, its fix closes the gap
  # and changes what the text says.
  MD037: false
  # Table pipe style, and pipe alignment. Both take their expected style from
  # the first table in a file, so one table decides for every other one, and a
  # single row brought into line flips the expectation and puts every remaining
  # table out. Neither changes what renders. A table whose first cell is empty
  # also cannot be written in the compact style most of these files use: the
  # row has to open with a pipe, which the rule then reads as a style break.
  #
  # MD056 stays on below: a row short of a cell silently drops data, which is
  # not a style question.
  MD055: false
  MD060: false
  # Duplicate headings, narrowed rather than turned off. A README that documents
  # two commands gives each an Example and a Usage under its own heading, which
  # the rule rejects by default because it compares against every heading in the
  # document. Restricted to siblings, it still catches the same name twice in
  # one section, which is the case that makes an anchor ambiguous.
  MD024:
    siblings_only: true

# The Markdown gate. Named .markdownlint-cli2.yaml in a repository, where both
# the workflow step and a bare local `markdownlint-cli2` read it.
#
# The file list lives here rather than in the step, which passes an empty
# `globs` so this one is used: a step naming its own glob leaves a local run
# checking a different set of files from the gate.

# What CI sees is the checkout, which is the tracked files and nothing else: no
# node_modules, no vendor/, no .venv, no build output. A working copy has all of
# them, so without this a local run reports hundreds of findings in third-party
# Markdown that the gate will never look at, and `--fix` rewrites it in place.
gitignore: true

globs:
  - "**/*.md"

# Read alongside gitignore above, which does not cover everything the checkout
# leaves out. A submodule is tracked as a commit rather than as files, so CI
# checks out an empty directory while a working copy holds the whole upstream
# tree; gitignore says nothing about it, and a repository that adds one names it
# here. node_modules is named because it is not gitignored in every repository
# that has one. The trailing `**` is what excludes a tree: a glob ending at the
# directory name matches nothing and is dropped silently.
#
# The agent directories and instruction files are excluded by the global
# gitignore rather than by a repository's own, and gitignore above reads only
# the ones in the tree. So CI, which checks out tracked files, never sees them,
# while a working copy holds them and would report findings the gate cannot.
ignores:
  - "**/node_modules/**"
  - ".agents/**"
  - ".claude/**"
  - ".codex/**"
  - AGENTS.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - GEMINI.md
  # the ergogen submodules, whose Markdown is upstream's. Matched at any depth:
  # each revision directory symlinks to the one checkout, so the same files are
  # reachable under v1/ through v4/ as well as at the path .gitmodules names.
  - "**/ergogen/footprints/**"
  - "**/ergogen/kb_ergogen_helper/**"

# Every rule markdownlint has, then what is given up and why.
config:
  # Line length, which defaults to 80. Tables and link-bearing prose here run
  # past any column worth setting, and rewrapping them buys nothing.
  MD013: false
  # Inline HTML. <kbd> marks up key names in the keybinding tables, and Markdown
  # has no equivalent, so this rule rejects correct markup rather than finding
  # anything wrong with it.
  MD033: false
  # Spaces inside emphasis. An asterisk here is usually a glob or a
  # multiplication sign, `*.glsl, *.glslp` and `Thickness * Width * Length`, and
  # the rule reads both as emphasis that someone padded. CommonMark does not:
  # neither closing asterisk is right-flanking, so none of it renders as
  # emphasis and there is nothing to correct. Left on, its fix closes the gap
  # and changes what the text says.
  MD037: false
  # Table pipe style, and pipe alignment. Both take their expected style from
  # the first table in a file, so one table decides for every other one, and a
  # single row brought into line flips the expectation and puts every remaining
  # table out. Neither changes what renders. A table whose first cell is empty
  # also cannot be written in the compact style most of these files use: the
  # row has to open with a pipe, which the rule then reads as a style break.
  #
  # MD056 stays on below: a row short of a cell silently drops data, which is
  # not a style question.
  MD055: false
  MD060: false
  # Duplicate headings, narrowed rather than turned off. A README that documents
  # two commands gives each an Example and a Usage under its own heading, which
  # the rule rejects by default because it compares against every heading in the
  # document. Restricted to siblings, it still catches the same name twice in
  # one section, which is the case that makes an anchor ambiguous.
  MD024:

"""The quiet half of the pipeline's log voice (the convention itself is at the top
of scripts/lib/common.sh).

A line that reports something happening, or something asking to be read, is a plain
print and always shows. A line that only confirms nothing needed doing goes through
`note` and shows only under PIPELINE_VERBOSE: a clean run of ten steps is otherwise
mostly the word "ok", and each step's closing OK: summary already carries the count
those lines would have added up to.

The switch is an environment variable rather than a flag because a run is a dozen
processes deep (wrappers calling helpers calling helpers), and every one of them
has to agree on how loud it is. `npm run pipeline -- -v` sets it for all of them;
see pipeline.sh. common.sh has the bash `note` for the wrappers.

Not an entry point: import it, do not run it.
"""

import os

VERBOSE = bool(os.environ.get("PIPELINE_VERBOSE"))


def note(line):
    """Print a line that only confirms nothing needed doing, under PIPELINE_VERBOSE.

    Takes the whole formatted line, so a call site reads the same as the print it
    replaced and the convention stays legible at the point of use."""
    if VERBOSE:
        print(line)

"""Shared helpers for the PCB provenance stamp.

The stamp is one string written into each generated PCB's title_block comment 1
at build time (see stamp-provenance.py) and checked by validate-provenance.py. Its
purpose is to detect when kicad/unrouted or kicad/routed have drifted from the
current ergogen config.yaml. Exactly one field is compared (config=); the rest is
human provenance and is never compared.

Format:
  splinter v=v4 built=2026-06-15T17:30:00Z config=a1b2c3d4e5f6 commit=bf4e6c2 clean=yes

  built=  ISO-8601 UTC build time (provenance)
  config= sha256(config.yaml bytes)[:12] -- the only compared field (the match key)
  commit= short git HEAD, or "unknown" outside a git tree (provenance)
  clean=  yes when the working tree was fully committed at build time, no when it
          had uncommitted changes, unknown outside a git tree (provenance)

This module is stdlib-only and imported by both the writer and the validator, so
the hashing and parsing stay identical on both sides.
"""

import hashlib
import re
import subprocess
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

STAMP_PREFIX = "splinter"
STAMP_COMMENT_INDEX = 0  # title_block "comment 1" is index 0


def write_stamp(board, text):
    """Store a stamp string in the board's title_block comment 1. Operates on an
    already-loaded pcbnew board (so this module stays stdlib-only / pcbnew-free),
    keeping the comment index in one place for every writer."""
    board.GetTitleBlock().SetComment(STAMP_COMMENT_INDEX, text)


def read_stamp(board):
    """Return the stamp string in an already-loaded board's title_block comment 1,
    or "" if it carries none. The counterpart to write_stamp, so every reader and
    writer shares the one comment index."""
    return board.GetTitleBlock().GetComment(STAMP_COMMENT_INDEX).strip()


def config_hash(config_path):
    """Return sha256 of the config file's bytes, truncated to 12 hex chars."""
    with Path(config_path).open("rb") as f:
        return hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()[:12]


def _git(*args):
    """Run a git command at the repo root (cwd) and return stripped stdout, or
    None if git is unavailable or the command fails (e.g. not a git tree)."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", *args],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=True,
        )
        return out.stdout.strip()
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        return None


def build_stamp(config_path, version):
    """Assemble the provenance stamp string for a freshly generated board.

    Only for a board built from config.yaml. Anything assembled out of boards that
    are already stamped inherits their stamp (read_stamp) instead: the git fields
    describe the tree at the moment they are read, so rebuilding a stamp later in a
    run would report on that moment rather than on the copper it is stamping."""
    commit = _git("rev-parse", "--short", "HEAD")
    status = _git("status", "--porcelain")
    if commit is None or status is None:
        commit, clean = "unknown", "unknown"
    else:
        clean = "yes" if status == "" else "no"
    built = datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    return f"{STAMP_PREFIX} v={version} built={built} config={config_hash(config_path)} commit={commit} clean={clean}"


def parse_config_field(comment_text):
    """Return the config= hash from a stamp string, or None if absent."""
    if not comment_text:
        return None
    m = re.search(r"\bconfig=([0-9a-f]+)\b", comment_text)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def silk_from_stamp(stamp):
    """Return the silkscreen form of a stamp: the full stamp minus the leading
    'splinter v=<ver> ' prefix, leaving 'built=... config=... commit=... clean=...'.
    The dropped prefix already rides the credit label on silk, so it is redundant
    there; the leading 'built=' field is what makes the silk text recognizable
    for idempotent re-stamping."""
    parts = stamp.split(" ", 2)
    return parts[2] if len(parts) == 3 else stamp

"""The two board stages, and the argument every validator uses to scope itself.

`unrouted/` is where routing is done and `routed/` holds the masters fab exports
from. Every validator runs over both by default and takes an optional positional
argument naming one, so this is the vocabulary plus the wiring that reads it.

It lives here rather than in each validator because the argparse call carries a
non-obvious workaround, and three copies of a workaround is three chances to fix
it in only two of them.

Not an entry point: import it, do not run it.
"""

STAGES = ("unrouted", "routed")


def add_stage_argument(parser, help_text):
    """Add the optional positional stage scope.

    default=None rather than list(STAGES): argparse validates the default against
    `choices` as well as the parsed values, and a list is not one of the choices,
    so a list default makes every no-argument run fail."""
    parser.add_argument("stages", nargs="*", choices=STAGES, default=None, help=help_text)


def selected(args):
    """The stages to run over: those named, or all of them."""
    return args.stages or list(STAGES)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assert kicad/unrouted and kicad/routed were built from the current config.yaml.

Reads the provenance stamp (title_block comment 1) from every working board and
runs two checks over it. Either failing exits nonzero, and fab runs this as a gate.

CURRENT. Each board's config= hash must equal a fresh hash of the active version's
config.yaml. A mismatch means the board was generated from a different config than
is on disk now (edit config, forgot to rebuild + re-route); a missing stamp means
the board predates stamping or was never built through ergogen.sh.

ONE RUN. Every board within a stage must carry the same stamp, not merely a
matching hash. stamp-provenance.py builds one stamp per run and writes it to every
board it is given, so equality here means the boards were built together. A half
restored or rebuilt on its own passes the hash check, since identical config bytes
hash identically across builds, and shows up only here. Compared within a stage and
never across one: unrouted/ legitimately carries a newer stamp than routed/ between
an ergogen run and the save back to the masters.

Active version comes from npm_package_config_VERSION, so run via npm:
  npm run validate:provenance

By default both stages are checked; pass stage names to narrow it (the fab gate
passes `routed`, since fab only consumes routed/ -- validating unrouted/
there would block a legitimate fab of a current routed master on unrelated
unrouted/ drift):
  validate-provenance.py routed
"""

import argparse
import collections
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from lib.pipeline_log import note
from lib.provenance import config_hash, parse_config_field
from lib.stages import add_stage_argument, selected

COMMENT1_RE = re.compile(r'\(comment\s+1\s+"([^"]*)"\)')


def stamped_text(pcb_path):
    """Return a board's whole stamp string, or "" if it carries none. Read from the
    file text rather than through pcbnew: this runs as a gate on every fab, and
    loading a board costs seconds where a regex costs milliseconds."""
    with Path(pcb_path).open(encoding="utf-8") as f:
        text = f.read()
    m = COMMENT1_RE.search(text)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    add_stage_argument(ap, "stage(s) to validate (default: both)")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--quiet",
        action="store_true",
        help="say nothing when every board passes (for use as a gate inside\n"
        "another step, which reports its own result)",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()
    stages = selected(args)

    version = os.environ.get("npm_package_config_VERSION")
    if not version:
        sys.exit("npm_package_config_VERSION not set -- run via npm (npm run validate:provenance)")

    config = f"{version}/ergogen/config.yaml"
    if not Path(config).is_file():
        sys.exit(f"ERROR {config}: not found")
    expected = config_hash(config)

    staged = {stage: sorted(Path(f"{version}/kicad/{stage}").glob("[!_]*.kicad_pcb")) for stage in stages}
    boards = [pcb for stage in stages for pcb in staged[stage]]
    if not boards:
        sys.exit(f"No boards under {version}/kicad/{{{','.join(stages)}}}/ to validate")

    stamps = {pcb: stamped_text(pcb) for pcb in boards}
    failures = 0
    for pcb in boards:
        stored = parse_config_field(stamps[pcb])
        if stored == expected:
            note(f"  ok {pcb}: config={stored}")
        elif stored is None:
            sys.stdout.flush()  # this line is stderr; keep it in step with the ok lines
            print(
                f"  MISSING {pcb}: no provenance stamp, rebuild to stamp",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            failures += 1
        else:
            sys.stdout.flush()
            print(
                f"  MISMATCH {pcb}: stamped config={stored}, current config={expected}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            failures += 1

    if failures:
        sys.stdout.flush()  # keep the ok lines above this summary under a pipe
        print(
            f"validate:provenance: {failures}/{len(boards)} board(s) stale or unstamped "
            f"for {version} (config={expected}). Rebuild, re-copy and re-route to clear",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    # Every board above hashes to the current config, so anything left here is a
    # stage whose boards were built in different runs (see ONE RUN in the docstring).
    split = [stage for stage in stages if len(set(map(stamps.get, staged[stage]))) > 1]
    if split:
        sys.stdout.flush()  # keep the ok lines above this report under a pipe
        for stage in split:
            by_stamp = collections.defaultdict(list)
            for pcb in staged[stage]:
                by_stamp[stamps[pcb]].append(pcb.name)
            print(
                f"  SPLIT {version}/kicad/{stage}/: boards were not built in one run",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            for text, names in sorted(by_stamp.items()):
                print(f"    {', '.join(names)}: {text}", file=sys.stderr)
        print(
            f"validate:provenance: {len(split)} stage(s) mix boards from different builds. "
            "The config hash cannot see this, since identical config bytes hash the same "
            "across builds. Re-run the pipeline so every board is built in one run",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)

    if not args.quiet:
        print(f"OK: validate:provenance: {len(boards)} board(s) match {config} (config={expected})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Every branch, not just main and pull requests: work lands on main directly as
# often as it arrives through one, so a check that only runs on main is a check
# that runs after the fact.
on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Keyed on the branch rather than the ref, so a re-push to one branch cancels
# its own earlier run and not another branch's. Keyed by the event as well: a
# cancelled run leaves its check runs on the head commit, and GitHub counts
# those against the required checks, so a push and its pull request cancelling
# each other would block the merge.
# Qualified by the repository the branch lives in, since a fork names its
# branches itself: two pull requests from different forks would otherwise share
# a group whenever they pick the same branch name.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name || github.repository }}-${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # six minutes, so a job still going at fifteen has hung rather than failed.

      - name: Set up Docker
